body:
_Migrated from issue #1141, filed 2026-07-26._

Found while repairing `mobile.spec.ts` for #1130 (#1140).

`cps` SPA, `frontend/src/pages/Catalog.tsx` ~line 689:

```tsx
<button aria-haspopup="true" aria-expanded={settingsOpen} aria-label={t('View settings')}>
...
{settingsOpen && <div className={styles.settingsMenu}>   {/* no role */}
```

`aria-haspopup="true"` is defined as equivalent to `aria-haspopup="menu"`. So a screen-reader user is told this button opens a **menu** — and the thing that opens has no role at all. `getByRole('menu')` finds nothing, which is exactly how this surfaced.

The panel contains toggle controls (currently the Discover section toggle, plus a second one added since), so the honest options are:

1. **`role="menu"` with `role="menuitemcheckbox"` children** — matches the promise, but brings the full menu keyboard contract (arrow-key roving focus, Escape, focus management) which is not implemented today. Claiming the role without the behaviour is worse than the current state.
2. **`aria-haspopup="dialog"` + `role="dialog"`** with a label and focus handling.
3. **Drop `aria-haspopup` and use `role="group"`** with `aria-label`, treating it as a disclosure rather than a menu — the smallest honest change, since a disclosure is what it actually is.

My read is (3): it is a small panel of independent toggles, not a command menu, and a disclosure pattern is what the markup already behaves like. But that is a design call with real consequences for assistive-tech users, so it should be a deliberate decision rather than something folded into a test repair.

Not blocking anything — noting it so the promise and the markup stop disagreeing.

Related: the a11y capability notes (SPA held at WCAG 2.2 AA); #1135 was a different instance of "the gate did not see it".
title: [a11y] View-settings popup promises a menu it does not provide
